# `nullable-removed`

null no longer allowed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `nullable-removed` (both directions), `nullable-removed-in-request`, `nullable-removed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`null` is no longer allowed.

## Why this default

In requests: clients sending null are rejected. In responses: clients no longer receive null, which is safe.

## Example

From test case [`nullable-removed`](../../test/cases/nullable-removed/): null no longer allowed in a request.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
        properties:
          name:
-           type:
-           - string
-           - 'null'
+           type: string
```

Findings:

- `nullable-removed-in-request` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  nullable-removed: info
```

## How to fix

In requests, keep accepting null.
